cues.en: The next real-world challenge is a tough one.
cues.zh: 下一個實務挑戰相當棘手。

cues.en: It's called filter bubbles, and it refers to societal problems that arise when all you show people are things that appeal to their existing interests.
cues.zh: 它叫做過濾泡泡，指的是當你只向人們展示符合既有興趣的內容時，所產生的社會問題。

cues.en: Let's say you're building a recommender system for a book store.
cues.zh: 假設你正在為書店建立推薦系統。

cues.en: If someone buys a book about a topic associated with right-wing politics, your recommender system will probably pick up on that, and start recommending more right-wing books to that person.
cues.zh: 如果有人買了右翼政治主題的書，推薦系統大概會捕捉到這點，開始向他推薦更多右翼書籍。

cues.en: If they respond to those recommendations, that person gets more and more immersed in right-wing ideology.
cues.zh: 如果他對這些推薦有反應，就會越來越沉浸在右翼意識形態裡。

cues.en: The same happens for someone who bought a book about left-wing politics.
cues.zh: 買了左翼政治書籍的人也一樣。

cues.en: The end result is that the recommender systems we developed to try and show people interesting things, creates a more polarized society.
cues.zh: 結果，我們原本為了向人們展示有趣事物而開發的推薦系統，卻創造出更兩極化的社會。

cues.en: This isn't something we ever anticipated in the early days of building recommender systems, but as the same techniques have been applied to social networks and advertising,
cues.zh: 在早期建立推薦系統時，我們完全沒有預料到這點。但當相同技術被應用到社群網路與廣告，

cues.en: it really has caused people to be exposed almost exclusively to things that reinforce their existing beliefs when they're online.
cues.zh: 它確實使人們上網時，幾乎只接觸到強化既有信念的內容。

cues.en: This is called a filter bubble because the content you're presenting your users is filtered in such a way that it keeps them within a bubble of their pre-existing interests.
cues.zh: 這叫做過濾泡泡，因為呈現給使用者的內容，經過篩選，使他們一直留在既有興趣的泡泡裡。

cues.en: The term arose in 2014 from Eli Pariser, and it proved to be a very prophetic observation.
cues.zh: 這個詞由 Eli Pariser 在 2014 年提出，後來證明是很有先見之明的觀察。

cues.en: He gave a TED Talk on it that you can look up if you want to hear more about it.
cues.zh: 他做過一場相關的 TED 演講，如果想了解更多，可以找來看。

cues.en: The tough thing is that this isn't necessarily bad from a business standpoint, but it's arguably very bad from an ethical standpoint.
cues.zh: 難處在於，這從商業角度未必是壞事，但從倫理角度，可以說非常糟糕。

cues.en: You've seen how to measure diversity in your recommendations, so you can actually quantify just how bubbly your recommendations are.
cues.zh: 你已經看過如何衡量推薦的多樣性，因此其實能量化推薦的泡泡程度。

cues.en: A little extra diversity in your recommendations can give people exposure to items that might help break them out of their bubble.
cues.zh: 讓推薦多一點多樣性，可以讓人們接觸可能幫助他們走出泡泡的項目。

cues.en: There's no easy solution, but making sure your business as whole doesn't rely too heavily on personalized content is a good start.
cues.zh: 沒有簡單的解法，但確保整個企業不過度依賴個人化內容，是很好的開始。

cues.en: Exposing items or content with broader, universal, objective appeal that resonate with the population as a whole, instead of certain subgroups, can help keep society unified.
cues.zh: 展示更廣泛、普遍、客觀地吸引大眾，能讓整體社會產生共鳴，而非只吸引特定群體的項目或內容，有助於維繫社會團結。

cues.en: It's a little hard to imagine that your recommender system might contribute to the downfall of civilization, but honestly, that's a question I've had to grapple with myself as an early practitioner in this field.
cues.zh: 很難想像，自己的推薦系統可能助長文明衰敗。但老實說，作為這個領域的早期實務工作者，這是我自己也必須掙扎思考的問題。

cues.en: And it's not fun to think about.
cues.zh: 這想起來並不愉快。

cues.en: We've talked a little bit in the past about user trust in your recommender system.
cues.zh: 先前已經稍微談過，使用者對推薦系統的信任。

cues.en: It's a good idea to make sure there are several recommendations that they recognize in their top-N results, to ensure they have some confidence that your system is producing relevant recommendations for them.
cues.zh: 最好確保 Top-N 結果中有幾個他們認得的推薦，讓他們相信系統能產生與自己相關的推薦。

cues.en: That way, they'll be more likely to explore the items you're recommending that they haven't heard of.
cues.zh: 如此一來，他們才更可能探索你推薦、但他們沒聽過的項目。

cues.en: There's a flipside to the trust problem as well, and that's what happens when a user that sees a recommendation that just makes them go, "Huh, why are you recommending that to me?"
cues.zh: 信任問題也有另一面：使用者看到某個推薦，只覺得「咦，為什麼推薦這個給我？」時，會發生什麼事？

cues.en: No matter how good your algorithm is, spurious results can creep in, and sometimes this can undermine a users' trust in your system as a whole.
cues.zh: 演算法再好，也可能混入不合理的結果，有時會破壞使用者對整個系統的信任。

cues.en: A good antidote to this is transparency, allow the user to see exactly why you recommended this item to them, and ideally, let them fix the root cause themselves.
cues.zh: 好的對策就是透明度：讓使用者清楚看到為什麼推薦這個項目，理想上，還能自行修正根本原因。

cues.en: It's a much better outcome if a user understands why you recommended something that they found confusing, and actually fixes the issue, than if they start posting on social media
cues.zh: 如果使用者能理解為什麼收到令他困惑的推薦，並真正修正問題，會比他開始在社群媒體上發文，

cues.en: about how horrible your company's recommendations are.
cues.zh: 抱怨你公司的推薦多糟糕，來得好多了。

cues.en: This example comes from Amazon's recommendations, where they recommend products from certain categories to me based on what they think my interests are.
cues.zh: 這個例子來自 Amazon 推薦：它根據對我興趣的推測，推薦某些類別的產品。

cues.en: I can click into the reasons why a given category was recommended, and see the specific items from my purchase history that led to the conclusion that I'm interested in this topic.
cues.zh: 我可以點進某個類別被推薦的原因，看到購買紀錄中的哪些特定項目，導致系統認為我對這個主題有興趣。

cues.en: If, for example, this category recommendation was based on items I had purchased as a gift for somebody else, I could exclude those items from my recommendations right here and now.
cues.zh: 例如，若這個類別推薦是根據我買給別人的禮物，就能當場把那些項目排除於推薦依據之外。

cues.en: So if I weren't actually a science fiction fan, instead of posting on Facebook about how wrong Amazon is about me, maybe I'd see that sci-fi related gift that I bought for my cousin here,
cues.zh: 所以如果我其實不是科幻迷，我可能會在這裡看到之前買給表親的科幻禮物，而不是去 Facebook 發文，說 Amazon 多不了解我，

cues.en: and understand why that recommendation happened, and I can fix the issue as well.
cues.zh: 然後理解為什麼會有這個推薦，也能修正問題。

cues.en: Of course, it's not always this easy.
cues.zh: 當然，不是每次都那麼容易。

cues.en: When you're dealing with more advanced algorithms such as deep learning or matrix factorization, you're basing recommendations on latent factors that can't easily be communicated to the user,
cues.zh: 處理深度學習或矩陣分解等較進階演算法時，推薦根據的是潛在因子，很難向使用者清楚說明，

cues.en: or even to you as a researcher, for that matter.
cues.zh: 其實甚至連身為研究人員的你，也不容易理解。

cues.en: That's part of why you don't see this sort of thing very often any more.
cues.zh: 這也是現在不太常看到這種功能的部分原因。

cues.en: Also, it's a lot of front end work to develop the user interfaces for tools like this, and it can be hard to justify the expense of developing it compared to all the other stuff your company needs to build.
cues.zh: 另外，開發這類工具的使用者介面，需要大量前端工作，與公司其他需要建置的功能相比，可能很難合理化開發成本。

cues.en: Still, all things being equal, transparency is a good thing for trust in your recommender system.
cues.zh: 不過在其他條件相同時，透明度對推薦系統的信任是好事。

cues.en: Another issue you'll deal with in the real world is outliers.
cues.zh: 實務上還會遇到離群值問題。

cues.en: Really, this is a concern for any machine learning system, not just for recommender systems.
cues.zh: 其實這是所有機器學習系統都要關心的，不只推薦系統。

cues.en: Your results are only as good as the data that you feed into it, and oftentimes, a lot of the work is in cleaning that input data, and filtering out outliers that might skew your results in unnatural ways.
cues.zh: 結果的好壞取決於送入的資料。很多時候，大部分工作是清理輸入資料，濾除可能以不自然方式扭曲結果的離群值。

cues.en: For example, imagine building a collaborative filtering system based on user rating behavior.
cues.zh: 例如，想像根據使用者評分行為建立協同過濾系統。

cues.en: What if some of the users in your data aren't actually real people at all, but are bots that are rating things in an unnatural manner?
cues.zh: 如果資料中的一些使用者根本不是真人，而是以不自然方式評分的機器人呢？

cues.en: A bot might also generate an excessively large number of ratings, and end up having a very large influence on your final recommendations.
cues.zh: 機器人也可能產生過量評分，最後對最終推薦造成非常大的影響。

cues.en: It's not always malicious behavior that you're up against, either.
cues.zh: 而且，你面對的不一定都是惡意行為。

cues.en: It might just be a web crawler that's polluting your data, or maybe even your own internal tools.
cues.zh: 可能只是網路爬蟲汙染資料，甚至可能是自家內部工具。

cues.en: Even among real people, you might want to filter some of them out.
cues.zh: 即使是真人，有些人你可能也想濾除。

cues.en: People who review items for a living will generate a large number of reviews, but their opinion shouldn't necessarily be that much more powerful than everyone else's.
cues.zh: 以評論項目維生的人，會產生大量評論，但他們的意見不一定應該比其他人強大那麼多。

cues.en: Another example is institutional buyers, who purchase large quantities of different items on behalf of companies.
cues.zh: 另一個例子是機構採購者，他們代表公司大量購買各種不同項目。

cues.en: Their behavior doesn't really reflect anyone's real interests, but they can have a huge influence on your recommendations if they aren't identified and filtered out.
cues.zh: 他們的行為並不真正反映任何人的實際興趣，但如果沒有辨識並濾除，就可能對推薦造成巨大影響。

cues.en: In most algorithms, a person with a large number of reviews will have an outsized influence on the recommendations your system makes.
cues.zh: 在大多數演算法中，評論數量很多的人，會對系統推薦產生不成比例的影響。

cues.en: So as with any machine learning system, you want to identify the outliers in your training data, understand them, and filter them out when appropriate.
cues.zh: 所以，和任何機器學習系統一樣，要辨識訓練資料中的離群值，了解它們，並在適當時濾除。
